findings.body:
**Complete process-group cleanup after the CLI leader exits.**

In `src/driver/claude-code/cli.ts:666`, cancellation delegates teardown to `terminateGracefully`. That helper returns when `child.close` settles (`src/shared/proc.ts:720-721`). If the CLI exits on SIGTERM but a same-group worker ignores SIGTERM and has redirected stdio, the worker survives. The SIGKILL rung never runs, and this invocation returns `aborted`.

Ensure cancellation also terminates surviving group members before teardown completes. As per path instructions, “tear down workers and release resources on abort so no spend or process survives the run.”
findings.title: Complete process-group cleanup after the CLI leader exits.

findings.body:
**Return the observed native session ID from the SDK transport.**

The SDK transport records the native `session_id` from init, assistant, and result frames, but the returned `WorkerResult` omits it. The object at `src/driver/claude-code/sdk.ts:865-884` includes only the store `sessionId` (line 878). It does not set `nativeSessionId` or `nativeSessionPath`, although `src/driver/types.ts:353-364` defines both for a lane that can observe the native ID. The CLI transport sets them (`src/driver/claude-code/cli.ts:988-997`).

For SDK runs, the job-finished session link therefore has no native ID. `src/kernel/runner.ts:300-316` builds result-derived links only from `nativeSessionId` and `nativeSessionPath` on the result, and `src/ops/review/internal/fixWorker.ts:507-512` reports the native ID only when `worker.nativeSessionId` is set. The ID remains only in the resume sidecar, written by `persistObservation` at `sdk.ts:1312`.

Set the native ID from the observation in the result:

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
       sessionId,
+      ...(observation.agentSessionId !== undefined && observation.agentSessionId !== ''
+        ? { nativeSessionId: observation.agentSessionId }
+        : {}),
       denials: observation.denials,
```

</details>

Derive `nativeSessionPath` with `nativeTranscriptPath` from the workspace, as `cli.ts:991-997` does, if archival depends on that field.
findings.title: Return the observed native session ID from the SDK transport.

findings.body:
**Report a caught dispatch failure as an error, even after a successful result.**

If the SDK stream yields a success result and then throws a non-abort error, the catch at `sdk.ts:614-616` records the failure. The verdict still derives its stop reason from the retained result at `sdk.ts:800`. `stopReasonOf` does not receive the recorded error, so it returns `complete` unless a budget or abort applies. The verdict then omits the error. It can also return `structuredOutput` when the schema accepts the retained payload.

Set the result status to `error` for a `dispatch-threw` failure. Also skip structured-output judgment for that failure. Otherwise a schema miss replaces the dispatch cause with an `output-invalid` error. Budget and abort precedence stay unchanged. The measured usage and the `dispatch-threw` cause still reach the verdict.

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
     const stopReason = stopReasonOf({
       aborted,
       harnessFailure: observation.harnessFailure !== undefined,
       maxTokens: budget.maxTokens,
       usage,
-      resultStatus: resultStatusOf(observation.result),
+      resultStatus:
+        observation.errorKind === 'dispatch-threw' ? 'error' : resultStatusOf(observation.result),
     });
```

```diff
     if (
       outputSchema !== undefined &&
       !aborted &&
       observation.harnessFailure === undefined &&
+      observation.errorKind !== 'dispatch-threw' &&
       observation.result !== undefined
     ) {
```
</details>
findings.title: Report a caught dispatch failure as an error, even after a successful result.
